argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrower certification defense than the initial audit frames. Aggregate readiness is positive because the current release clears launch readiness by 2.5 percentage points and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, which supports launch readiness on the whole. The limiting fact is the current developer-support migration regression, which is a named use-case weakness. Under the policy text, that weakness does not bar certification if it is explicitly disclosed in current release documentation or covered by approved mitigation. Because the record does not show approved mitigation or accepted risk, the supportable position is caveated certification tied to explicit current model-card disclosure of the limitation, not an unqualified claim that certification is already cleanly satisfied.
claims_about_business_cost: No separate business-cost claim is needed to resolve the audit question. The admissible basis for minimizing escalation is that the aggregate readiness evidence is positive and the remaining issue is a bounded documentation-and-disclosure condition rather than a demonstrated launch-blocking safety failure.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not let prior approval or informal monitoring substitute for current release evidence. It does allow certification when current evaluation results are reflected and material segment weaknesses are disclosed or covered by approved mitigation. On this record, the only supportable path is disclosure-based certification rather than treating the stale approval or monitoring comment as satisfying the policy.
concessions: The current record does not evidence that the required disclosure has already been completed for the current release.
The current record does not contain approved mitigation or signed risk acceptance covering the developer-support migration weakness.
Prior approval of the same model family and the release-thread monitoring comment are contextual only and do not satisfy the policy requirement.
